terms.definition: Says 'is not' or 'am not' in a sentence that has no verb, like 'I'm not busy'.
terms.example: لَسْتُ مَشْغُولًا الآنَ، تَفَضَّلْ. — I'm not busy now, go ahead.
terms.discussion: It changes with the person: لَسْتُ (I), لَسْتَ (you), لَيْسَتْ (she). The next word takes the ـًا ending: مَشْغُولًا.
terms.anti_example: Not 'لَا أَنَا مَشْغُولٌ' for 'I'm not busy': لَا goes with verbs. Say 'لَسْتُ مَشْغُولًا'.

terms.definition: There is, there are: tells you something exists in a place.
terms.example: هُنَاكَ مَقْهًى صَغِيرٌ قُرْبَ بَيْتِي. — There's a small café near my house.
terms.discussion: Standing alone, it also means 'over there'. For 'there isn't', say لَيْسَ هُنَاكَ.

terms.definition: Wanting to do something: put a present-tense verb right after أَنْ.
terms.example: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ طَاوِلَةً لِشَخْصَيْنِ. — I want to book a table for two.
terms.anti_example: 'أُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ' means 'I want him to go'. For yourself, both verbs are 'I': 'أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ'.
